solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top entertainer from Ramsgate, originally

indicators.note: the letters of the town's name are taken back to an earlier, unformed state and rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A star performer who hails from the Kent seaside town of Ramsgate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like it is about where the star was born, but it signals that RAMSGATE is rearranged. Ramsgate is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer at the very top of the profession is a huge celebrity, a synonym.

clue.text: Manager initially wants top-class staff in office

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Manager is used

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-rate

explanation.surface: A boss insists on hiring only the best people for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a ceremonial rod carried as a symbol of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod borne before an official, such as the one in Parliament, is a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Good opportunity for someone at wedding

parts.note: room, as in room for improvement, means scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A wedding is a chance to meet people.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridegroom is one of the two principal people at any marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Vastly superior ways shown by a school principal

parts.note: streets are roads or ways
the head is the headteacher of a school

explanation.surface: A head teacher shows the way to excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means far better than the rivals, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Help given in class is timely

indicators.note: the letters are supplied within the words class is timely, running across them

explanation.surface: Classroom help that arrives at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is a plain synonym, as a verb.

clue.text: Performs in another comedy that's successful at the start

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the four words another comedy that's successful is taken

explanation.surface: An actor appears in yet another hit comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform on stage is to play a part, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Girl of firm character, mostly

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: a letter of the alphabet is a character

explanation.surface: A young woman with a strong, determined personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' seems to mean personality, but it is a written letter, cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female forename, best known from the French novelist.

clue.text: Wet day at the weekend, and clergyman's forgotten hat

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday

indicators.note: the topmost letter, the head of the word, is left off

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A rainy weekend, and a vicar left his hat behind.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first letter sits on top, so losing its 'hat' removes the C of CURATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something through completely is to make it thoroughly wet, used as a verb.

clue.text: Artist is victorious in local election?

parts.note: a party that gains a seat is victorious in it
a borough is a town council area contested at local elections

explanation.surface: A painter wins a seat at a council election.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter; the clue splits his name into a party taking a council area.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English painter, an example of the class.

clue.text: Almost axe Irish singing group

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to chop is to axe

explanation.surface: An Irish vocal ensemble is nearly cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers, such as one in a church, is a choral group.

clue.text: Try swallowing entire onion-like plant

indicators.note: one word takes the other into its middle, as if eating it

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or try
all means the whole, entire

explanation.surface: Attempting to eat a whole onion in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small bulb related to the onion, used in cooking.

clue.text: Impressionist painter's room refurbished

indicators.note: a refurbished room is done up anew, so these letters are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: An Impressionist artist's studio gets a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' looks like a painter such as Monet, but it is a mimic of voices.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer who mimics famous people does impressions of them.

clue.text: Roast meat briefly, and cover with fat when cooking

indicators.note: the word is cut short, its last letter removed

parts.note: lamb is a meat
to baste is to spoon fat over meat while it cooks

explanation.surface: Instructions for roasting a joint of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' looks like a cooking verb, but it means to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them severely, the same as to berate.

clue.text: A couple of cents service charge

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for a cent, so two of them make CC
use, as in of service or of use, means service

explanation.surface: A small service charge of two cents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee, but it is the verb to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a crime is to formally blame them, a synonym.

clue.text: Mountaineer rose, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a rose can be a plant that grows up a wall or trellis

explanation.surface: A mountaineer, or perhaps a rose?
explanation.definitionFit: A person who scales peaks, and also a plant that grows upward on supports, such as a rambling rose.

clue.text: Missing worker has caught terrible disease

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it, as if catching it

parts.note: a worker ant is the usual crossword worker
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: An employee is off work with a nasty illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is away, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Kid beginning to understand a book of the Old Testament

parts.note: to josh is to kid or tease

indicators.note: only the opening letter of understand is taken

explanation.surface: A child starts to grasp a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sixth book of the Hebrew Bible, named after Moses's successor.

clue.text: Novel souvenir of seaside trip

definitions.meaning: a book by Graham Greene, published 1938
a stick of hard pink sweet with lettering through it, sold at the resort on the Sussex coast

explanation.surface: A souvenir from a day by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the Graham Greene book. Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast, and rock is a hard stick sweet sold there.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both Greene's novel and the stick of hard candy bought at the south-coast resort.

clue.text: Something added to sauce for a lark

definitions.meaning: a pickled flower bud put in sauces such as tartare
a lark is a prank or escapade

explanation.surface: Adding something to a sauce just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickled bud used as flavouring, and also a frolic or playful escapade.

clue.text: Before surgical procedure, doctor offers small amount to drink

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A doctor offers a patient a little drink before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity of liquid, as in just a sip, is a small amount.

clue.text: Two bishops joining Salvation Army at far end of church … now?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two make BB

indicators.note: only the final letter of church is taken

explanation.surface: Two bishops join the Salvation Army at the back of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: with the clue read through, it is the day of worship when a churchgoer is in church now.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of rest and worship is when worshippers are in church, so the clue asks if this is that day.

clue.text: Superior meal with no starter

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped, a play on a meal without its first course

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine dinner served without a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher in rank or position, as in the higher classes, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Noble Lear, ruined

indicators.note: the name is wrecked and its letters rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear brought to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking below a marquess is a nobleman.

clue.text: Was female at university a kitchen employee?

parts.note: her is a female pronoun
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Did a woman at college work in a kitchen?
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to clean dishes is a dishwasher in a restaurant kitchen.
